chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn Abī al-Ṣahbān, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥammād, from Ibrāhīm ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Abī Usāmah al-Shaḥḥām, who said:

A man said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “Should I delay the maghrib until the stars become clearly visible?” He said: “That is Khattābiyyah. Indeed, Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام brought it down to Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم when the disk had set.”

key_terms.الْمَغْرِبَ: the maghrib salat (prayer), the sunset prayer
key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلَ: Jibrāʾīl, the angel who conveyed revelation
key_terms.خَطَّابِيَّةٌ: a reference to the Khattabiyyah sect or their view
key_terms.سَقَطَ الْقُرْصُ: the sun’s disk has set below the horizon

ai.seo_question: Should maghrib salat (prayer) be delayed until the stars appear?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses the time of maghrib salat (prayer) and rejects delaying it until the stars become visible. It states that the prescribed time was conveyed by Jibrāʾīl عليه السلام to the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم at the setting of the sun’s disk, establishing the ruling for the prayer’s onset.
